messages:
kevin (Acme): Hi, ran a pinned upgrade this morning and our embeddings output width changed mid-run. Was pinned to open-embed-1024, now some responses are 1536 wide. No 4xx/5xx, just wrong vector length.

alice (Support): Sorry to hear that — can you paste a sample request/response (sanitized) and the model value you pinned to?

kevin (Acme): Sure — we pin via the API param model: \"open-embed-1024:stable\". Example request: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT' -d '{"model":"open-embed-1024:stable","input":["foo","bar"],"batch_size":8}'``` Response shows vectors length 1536 for input[1]. Request id in header x-request-id: rq_0a1b2c3d.

sam (Cust-Eng): Do you pull from a VPC/private deploy or hosted? Also do you have client-side caching or a proxy that might merge variants?

kevin (Acme): Hosted API. No caching on our side, single thread generating embeddings, batched on our side (batch_size 8). We saw it start after a routine pinned update yesterday.

ops-bot: [router] request rq_0a1b2c3d matched routing policy: region=us-west, customer_tier=standard, model_requested=open-embed-1024:stable -> selected_model=open-embed-1536-compat (fallback due to variant-mapping rule).

maria (SRE): That bot log is interesting — looks like a routing fallback substituted a compatible variant. We recently added a heuristic to substitute when quantization/profile mismatch is detected. Would you be able to run a quick repro with the exact request and the header `x-request-id` so we can trace?

alice (Support): For immediate mitigation you can pin to the model digest (full hash) instead of the tag; that bypasses variant substitution. Eg `model: \"open-embed-1024@sha256:abcd1234ef...\"`. Can you try one request with that and paste the response?

kevin (Acme): Trying now. Will post results.

kevin (Acme): Result: using the digest returns vectors length 1024 as expected. So tagging/tag-resolution/fallback is the culprit. When we used the tag it returned 1024 sometimes and 1536 other times.

sam (Cust-Eng): OK that nails it. Likely a routing rule that picks a higher-capacity embed variant when backend capacity or quantization mismatch flag flips. That should not change vector dimensionality — escalating to eng-runtime.

eng-runtime-oncall: thanks for the trace, we're pulling logs for rq_0a1b2c3d and surrounding minutes. Can you also share the customer account id and whether you saw this across multiple users/batches?

kevin (Acme): Account id: acct-8821. It happened across ~3 different batch calls in a 2 minute window. Not all requests were affected.

maria (SRE): Notes for runtime: check variant-substitution history for open-embed-1024:stable between ts 3419256700-3419256900; verify the substitution preserves embedding schema or else block substitution for embed endpoints.

alice (Support): Closing loop: suggested immediate actions for customer: 1) Pin to exact digest. 2) If you rely on tag resolution, set strict_model_schema=true in request to reject mismatched variants (we can enable a safety flag). I'll follow up with an internal ticket to change default behavior.

kevin (Acme): Appreciate it — digest pin is a fine workaround, but please keep me posted on permanent fix.

alice (Support): Will do — opened INC-embed-variant-schema-412 and pinged runtime/routers. :thumbsup:
